newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds tread water ahead of US data, holiday.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds tread water ahead of US data, holiday.

text.p: Emerging market debt hovered directionless ahead of the June U.S. employment report and the Independence Day holiday on Friday, analysts said on Thursday.
"The market is directionless ahead of payrolls this afternoon and the big U.S. holiday on Friday," an emerging market analyst said.
A Reuters consensus of economists' forecasts expected non-farm payrolls -- expected at 1230 GMT -- to rise to 222,000 versus a previous 138,000 in May.
BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said he expected a "spurt of activity" after the numbers, after which players would square their positions ahead of the long weekend.

"If the number is smaller than expected, then we expect a rally followed by a selloff. If the number is larger than expected, then we expect a selloff and then for dealers to buy back their shorts," Gray said.
Dealers said they expected the London market to work a half-day on Friday in the light of the U.S. holiday.
"EMTA (Emerging markets traders' association) were thinking of calling a market halt but we reckon the Russians will be in (on Friday) so if anything a half-day," a dealer said.
EMTA recommended that the emerging debt markets in the U.S. should remain open for business until 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Thursday July 3, and should be closed on Friday, July 4.
